acceptance_checks: scripts/shiki_contracts.py defines a single plan-task runtime resolver that returns the `runtime` value when only `runtime` is present, the `assigned_runtime` value when only `assigned_runtime` is present, that same value when both are present and EQUAL, and None when neither key is present.
That resolver raises a ValueError subclass whose message names both keys and both values when a task entry declares `runtime` and `assigned_runtime` with DIFFERENT values.

scripts/shiki_contracts.py also exposes a task-capability helper derived from shiki_runtime_registry (roles intersecting TASK_RUNTIME_ROLES), and `bash scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh` passes with shiki_tasks, validate_shiki and mergegate_check all importing from it.
register_task_from_plan with a task entry {"runtime": "codex", ...} writes assigned_runtime == "codex".
register_task_from_plan with a task entry {"assigned_runtime": "codex", ...} writes assigned_runtime == "codex". (Measured before the change: "claude-code".)
register_task_from_plan with a task entry declaring NEITHER key writes assigned_runtime == "claude-code".
register_task_from_plan with {"runtime": "claude"} and with {"assigned_runtime": "claude"} each raise ShikiError naming the value 'claude' and the accepted task-capable runtime names.
That refusal happens BEFORE any mirror write: after the raise, the target's .shiki/tasks/ and .shiki/ledger/ each contain no new file. A test asserts the directory contents, not just the exception.
The literal "runtime" no longer appears inside the body of register_task_from_plan; the resolver call is the only place a plan-entry runtime key is read.
require_grilled_plan raises ShikiError for a plan whose task entry declares a runtime that is not task-capable under EITHER key, naming the task index, the offending value and the accepted names.
require_grilled_plan raises ShikiError for a plan whose task entry declares both keys with different values.

validate_plan in scripts/validate_shiki.py raises ValidationError for a mirror plan whose task entry declares a non-task-capable value under the `runtime` key, and for one declaring both keys with different values. It does NOT validate the `assigned_runtime` value, and a comment at the check names .shiki/plans/P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792.json as the reason.

.shiki/schemas/plan.schema.json's task item declares `runtime` with an enum set-equal to .shiki/schemas/task.schema.json's assigned_runtime enum, and declares `assigned_runtime` as {"type": "string"} with a description marking it the accepted alias.

Every plan under .shiki/plans/ still passes the mirror schema-conformance loop after the schema change (measured today: 0 failures for exactly this shape; enumerating `assigned_runtime` instead yields 1 failure on P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792).

cmd_plan_guide's plan_contract gains an optional_task_fields entry naming `runtime` with its accepted values plus non_goals, dependencies, locks, risk_level, required_skills, test_command, expected_branch, expected_pr and github_issue, and does NOT name cca_checklist_profile.

mergegate_check._frozen_task_match_errors resolves the frozen plan's runtime through the shared resolver, so a frozen entry declaring `assigned_runtime: "codex"` against a claude-code task yields the same mismatch error a `runtime`-declaring entry yields today. (Measured before the change: 0 errors vs 1 error for the two forms.)
A frozen task entry declaring both keys with different values, or declaring a non-task-capable value, yields a blocking reason from _frozen_task_match_errors - never an uncaught exception.
_FROZEN_TASK_MATCH_FIELDS in scripts/mergegate_check.py is byte-unchanged.

tests/test_paired_invariants.py gains a binder asserting the plan.schema.json task-item `runtime` enum is SET-EQUAL to the task.schema.json assigned_runtime enum, in the module's existing style, with a divergence test that fails on a mutated copy and a message naming both files.

tests/test_paired_invariants.py gains a binder asserting the record key sets emitted by register_task_from_plan and cmd_issue_plan are SET-EQUAL, with a divergence test that fails on a mutated copy and a message naming both functions.

The new behavioural tests live in tests/test_plan_runtime_key.py, and each behavioural assertion is paired with a divergence assertion that feeds the old code path the same input and asserts the old wrong answer.
tests/test_plan_runtime_key.py fails when register_task_from_plan is reverted to `task_plan.get("runtime", "claude-code")`, and the failure message names scripts/shiki_contracts.py and the resolver.
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests passes. (Baseline before the change: Ran 1177 tests, OK.)
python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target . passes.
bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh, bash scripts/test_shiki_run_orchestrator.sh and bash scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh all pass.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
non_goals: Do not change scripts/shiki_cli.py's hardcoded --runtime choices (line 355), even though they are missing `codex-front`, which 9 live tasks use.
Do not remove `github-actions` from .shiki/schemas/task.schema.json's assigned_runtime enum, even though no runtime-registry role permits it on a task.
Do not make register_task_from_plan or cmd_issue_plan carry cca_checklist_profile; that is the sibling slice, kept out of this one by the operator's 2026-08-22 decision.
Do not edit, correct or reserialize any plan under .shiki/plans/, and in particular not the spec-frozen P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792.json.
Do not restructure _FROZEN_TASK_MATCH_FIELDS into a field-name mapping.
Do not promote any task field to required in task.schema.json or validate_shiki.TASK_REQUIRED.
Do not add a SADR, a target ADR, or a CONTEXT.md entry.
Do not change shiki_locks matching semantics, the runtime registry's descriptors, or any adapter.
scope:
In scripts/shiki_contracts.py (a leaf module that imports only json, pathlib and shiki_runtime_registry, and that mergegate_check, validate_shiki and shiki_tasks can all import without a cycle), add ONE shared resolver for a plan task entry's declared runtime, plus a task-capability helper built on the runtime registry. The resolver is the single authority on which key names a plan may use: it prefers `runtime`, falls back to `assigned_runtime`, returns None when neither is present, returns the shared value when both are present and equal, and raises a ValueError subclass naming both keys and both values when both are present and differ. Its docstring records the decision and its reason: `runtime` is canonical (73 of 79 existing plan task entries use it, and the handoff surface emits `runtime` at shiki_tasks.py:590/:1210/:1235), `assigned_runtime` is the accepted alias because a planner reaching for the task record's own field name is the mistake that actually happened, and honouring a declared value beats silently defaulting.

In scripts/shiki_tasks.py, replace `task_plan.get("runtime", "claude-code")` at line 340 with a resolver call, and validate the resolved value against the runtime registry BEFORE any mirror write. register_task_from_plan currently calls append_ledger before write_json, so an unknown runtime must raise before the ledger append or a refusal leaves an orphan ledger entry behind. The `claude-code` default applies only when the resolver returns None. Extend require_grilled_plan with the same resolution and validation so `shiki plan ingest` / `shiki run` refuse a plan carrying an unknown runtime or a conflicting key pair, naming the task index, the offending value and the accepted names. Extend cmd_plan_guide's `plan_contract` with an `optional_task_fields` block naming `runtime` and its accepted values alongside the other fields registration actually carries; do NOT name cca_checklist_profile, which registration still drops (that is a separate slice).

In scripts/validate_shiki.py, extend validate_plan to reject a task entry whose `runtime` value is not task-capable and to reject a conflicting key pair. Deliberately do NOT validate the `assigned_runtime` VALUE here: validate_plan runs repo-wide over the mirror, and the spec-frozen .shiki/plans/P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792.json declares `assigned_runtime: "claude"` (not a registry runtime at all) on a goal that is already complete. That plan is an approval-bearing frozen artifact and must never be edited, so a mirror-wide alias-value check would turn the repository red with no legal remedy. Measured: a `runtime`-value check and a key-conflict check each break 0 of the 33 mirror plans; an `assigned_runtime`-value check breaks exactly that one. Put the reason in a comment at the check, naming that plan.

In .shiki/schemas/plan.schema.json, declare the task item's `runtime` with an enum set-equal to .shiki/schemas/task.schema.json's `assigned_runtime` enum, and declare `assigned_runtime` as {"type": "string"} with a description marking it the accepted alias. The asymmetry is deliberate and load-bearing for the same reason as above: measured, this exact shape produces 0 mirror schema-loop failures, while enumerating `assigned_runtime` produces `$.tasks[0].assigned_runtime: value 'claude' is not one of [...]` on the frozen plan.

In scripts/mergegate_check.py, route the bespoke runtime check below the _FROZEN_TASK_MATCH_FIELDS loop (lines 451-458) through the same resolver, so a frozen plan entry declaring the alias binds exactly as one declaring `runtime` does today. Leave _FROZEN_TASK_MATCH_FIELDS itself byte-unchanged: its loop compares identically-named fields and restructuring it into a name mapping is churn on a governance-critical constant. The gate must degrade to a blocking reason, never an uncaught exception, when a frozen entry declares a conflicting key pair or a non-task-capable value.

In tests/test_paired_invariants.py, add two binders in the module's existing style (each with a `*_holds` test pinning the live agreement and a `*_divergence_*` test proving the binder fails on a mutated copy, with failure messages naming BOTH sites and the fix): the plan-schema `runtime` enum set-equal to the task-schema `assigned_runtime` enum, and the record key sets emitted by register_task_from_plan and cmd_issue_plan set-equal to each other. The second is the durable guard for this defect class: the two paths emit byte-identical key sets today and nothing asserts it, so the next one-path-only field would land as silently as this one did.

In tests/test_plan_runtime_key.py (new), cover the resolver, the registration carry, the pre-ledger refusal, the ingest refusal, and the gate binding. Pair each behavioural assertion with a divergence assertion that feeds the OLD code path the same input and asserts the old wrong answer, so the suite proves it detects the regression rather than merely passing today.

REPRODUCIBILITY - what this task must reproduce and then fix, measured 2026-08-24 against the real scripts/ modules:
  register_task_from_plan({"assigned_runtime": "codex", ...}) -> task assigned_runtime == 'claude-code'   (plan value dropped)
  that task through shiki_runtime.validate_task_runtime_for_execution -> PASSES (dispatches to Claude Code, silently)
  register_task_from_plan({"runtime": "codex", ...})          -> task assigned_runtime == 'codex'         (correct)
  _frozen_task_match_errors(task=claude-code, frozen={"assigned_runtime": "codex"}) -> []                 (gate blind)
  _frozen_task_match_errors(task=claude-code, frozen={"runtime": "codex"})          -> 1 error
  shiki_schema.validate_instance(plan_with_assigned_runtime, plan.schema.json)      -> accepted (additionalProperties: true)
Baseline suite before the change: `Ran 1177 tests in 130.114s / OK`.
